def match(pattern: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Implements a regular expression matching algorithm that supports literal characters,
    '.' (which matches any single character), '*' (which matches zero or more of the 
    preceding element), and '+' (which matches one or more of the preceding element).
    The algorithm uses an iterative approach with two pointers to traverse the pattern 
    and text strings simultaneously.
    """
    p_len, t_len = len(pattern), len(text)
    p_index, t_index = 0, 0
    star_index, match_index = -1, 0

    while t_index < t_len:
        if p_index < p_len and (pattern[p_index] == text[t_index] or pattern[p_index] == '.'):
            p_index += 1
            t_index += 1
        elif p_index < p_len and pattern[p_index] == '*':
            star_index = p_index
            match_index = t_index
            p_index += 1
        elif star_index != -1:
            p_index = star_index + 1
            t_index = match_index + 1
            match_index += 1
        else:
            return False

    while p_index < p_len and pattern[p_index] == '*':
        p_index += 1

    return p_index == p_len
